svg.title: 4. Scenario: flash sale traffic spike
svg.text: What went wrong last year (and the fix)
Scenario: the 12:00 flash sale, 20x traffic in 90 seconds
Every layer exists to make sure the layer behind it sees less traffic, at a steadier rate. Numbers are requests per second at the peak.
SKU is a counter: a Lua
Load that reaches each layer (share of the 120,000 req/s peak)
Load test at 2x the forecast peak, with the real WAF rules on
Ask for limit increases: Lambda concurrency, EC2 vCPU, DynamoDB
Add Aurora readers; set DynamoDB warm throughput on carts
Raise HPA minReplicas and Karpenter headroom; warm caches
Watch queue age, p99 checkout, 5xx at the ALB, Valkey CPU
Put the minimums back, let Karpenter consolidate
Connections ran out at 1,800 and every pod retried. Fix: RDS Proxy, a queue in front of order writes, and retries with jitter.
Stock was checked in SQL with SELECT then UPDATE.
Two shoppers bought the last unit. Fix: one conditional UPDATE (or a Valkey DECR) so the check and the write are the same step.
Karpenter needed 3 minutes for new nodes.
The spike was over in 2. Fix: scale before the sale, keep low-priority pause pods as headroom that real pods evict.
The CDN cached a 503 for 60 s.
Fix: short error-caching TTLs on CloudFront and an origin failover group to a static "sold out" page in S3.
CPU looked fine while the queue age climbed to 9 minutes. Fix: alarm on ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage and on p99, not on CPU.
